name: YF-S401 water flow sensor (hall-effect, pulse output)
description: Small hall-effect water flow meter: water spins a magnetic rotor past a hall-effect sensor, and the signal wire gives a square wave (50 % +/- 10 % duty) of F = 98 x Q Hz for Q in L/min (+/- 2 %), i.e. 5880 pulses per litre. Rated 0.3-6 L/min, supply DC 4.5/5-24 V at up to 15 mA; the pulse high level is close to the supply (> 4.7 V at 5 V), so a 3.3 V board needs a divider or level shifter on the signal. Sold as: YF-S401 1/4 inch (6 mm hose barb) water flow sensor with 3 flying leads, red VCC, yellow OUT signal, black GND.
eli5: A tiny water wheel in a pipe that blinks a signal faster the faster water flows, so your board can measure how much water passes.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Red wire: supply, DC 5-24 V (4.5 V minimum); feed it from the board's 5 V pin

pins.name: OUT
pins.description: Yellow wire: pulse output, F = 98 x Q Hz (Q in L/min); high level about the supply voltage (> 4.7 V at 5 V), so it goes to a 3.3 V GPIO through a 10 kOhm / 20 kOhm divider (Sparkbench adds it)

supplierQuery: YF-S401 water flow sensor hall effect 0.3-6L/min
buildNotes: Wires: red = VCC (5-24 V), yellow = OUT pulse signal, black = GND.
Flow Q [L/min] = F [Hz] / 98; one litre = 5880 pulses. Count rising edges with a pin interrupt over a fixed window.

The signal swings to about the supply voltage (> 4.7 V at 5 V). On an ESP32 or Pico put a divider (10 kOhm from OUT to the GPIO, 20 kOhm from the GPIO to GND) or a level shifter in the signal line; never wire it straight to a 3.3 V GPIO.
Mount it with the arrow in the flow direction and within 5 degrees of vertical; below about 0.3 L/min the rotor may not turn and accuracy is poor.
The 98 Hz per L/min factor is +/- 2 % nominal; for accurate volume, time a known amount of water into a jug and adjust the factor.

driver.code:
# YF-S401 hall-effect water flow sensor, MicroPython driver.
# A magnet on the rotor passes a hall-effect sensor; the yellow OUT wire gives a
# square wave (50 % +/- 10 % duty) whose frequency follows the flow:
#   F [Hz] = 98 * Q [L/min]  (+/- 2 %)   ->  5880 pulses per litre
# Rated flow 0.3-6 L/min. Supply 4.5/5-24 V DC (red wire), 15 mA at 5 V.
# The output high level is about the supply (> 4.7 V at 5 V), so on a 3.3 V
# board (ESP32, Pico) put a divider or level shifter between OUT and the GPIO.
from machine import Pin
import time

HZ_PER_LPM = 98          # datasheet: F = 98 * Q
PULSES_PER_LITRE = HZ_PER_LPM * 60   # 5880


class YFS401:
    def __init__(self, pin, hz_per_lpm=HZ_PER_LPM, pull=None):
        """pin: GPIO number (or Pin) wired to OUT (yellow). hz_per_lpm: the
        K factor, 98 from the datasheet; calibrate it with a measuring jug for
        better accuracy. pull: e.g. Pin.PULL_UP if your wiring needs it."""
        if isinstance(pin, int):
            pin = Pin(pin, Pin.IN, pull) if pull is not None else Pin(pin, Pin.IN)
        self.pin = pin
        self.k = hz_per_lpm
        self._count = 0
        self.pin.irq(handler=self._edge, trigger=Pin.IRQ_RISING)

    def _edge(self, pin):
        self._count += 1

    def pulses(self):
        """Rising edges counted since start or reset()."""
        return self._count

    def reset(self):
        self._count = 0

    def litres(self):
        """Total volume since start or reset(), in litres."""
        return self._count / (self.k * 60)

    def flow(self, window_ms=1000):
        """Count pulses for window_ms and return the flow rate in L/min."""
        start = self._count
        t0 = time.ticks_ms()
        time.sleep_ms(window_ms)
        n = self._count - start
        dt = time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), t0)
        if dt <= 0:
            return 0.0
        hz = n * 1000 / dt
        return hz / self.k

example.code:
from yfs401 import YFS401

sensor = YFS401({OUT})
while True:
    q = sensor.flow(1000)
    print('Q=%.1f L/min' % q)
